IncidentBot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 'priority-hotshot' p99 latency > SLO threshold (3.2s) — paging oncall
Ana M.: seeing huge queue depth on pool 'priority-hotshot' since 12:02 UTC. p95 ~ 600ms, p99 ~ 3.2s. streaming stalls on a subset of sessions
Mike R.: oncall here, looking. Any changes deployed around 11:50?
Sylvie: not from runtime team. We rolled model quantization config for some clusters at 10:30 but different pool. Could be autoscaler flapping
Jordan: getting logs — handshake timeouts during shard attach: `WARN handshake timeout for slot 42, waited 12s`
Devon: autoscaler metrics show scale-up requests from scheduler, but warmup failures: `warmup_success_rate=0.28` on that pool
Ana M.: customer impact: 4 customers with active Dedicated reservations reported streaming stalls and token dropouts. CS reports 2 customers saw degraded throughput on prod region us-west-2
Mike R.: can we route traffic to standby pool? Policy allows fallback to 'priority-fallback' but payload shape matters (streaming vs non-streaming)
Sylvie: standby pool lacks same GPU class; may increase latency but avoid stalls. Preparing canary route command
Oncall-SRE: manual mitigation steps per runbook: 1) try manual slot-attach 2) enable fallback routing 3) increase oversubscribe throttle
Ana M.: running manual slot-attach for 3 slots now: `./infractl attach-slot --pool priority-hotshot --count 3` — logs: `attach started id=att-891`
Jordan: attach started but observed `kv-cache-miss` spike coincident. KV miss ratio from 0.02 -> 0.4
Devon: warmup logs show model weights streaming slow from object storage on those hosts: `FETCH chunk 128KB took 1.6s` — likely IO bottleneck during burst
Mike R.: that matches autoscale delay: nodes provisioned but warmup stalled waiting for weights. That's why requests queue up and p99 spikes
Ana M.: applying immediate fallback: enabling route to 'priority-fallback' for streaming only. Command: `routes set --from pool:priority-hotshot --to pool:priority-fallback --filter streaming`
Sylvie: fallback enabled. Traffic shifting 20% -> fallback now. Monitoring p99
Jordan: p99 drop starting to show: 3.2s -> 1.1s in the last minute for streaming. But queue depth still high (avg 1800)
Devon: continuing attachment. attach att-891 progressed to `state=done` for 2/3 slots, 1 failing with `fetch timeout`
Ana M.: can we increase warmup parallelism? runtime flag `--warmup-parallel=6` might help; production default is 2
Sylvie: I can push toggle to 6 on the pool but need rapid approval. Mike? @Mike R.
Mike R.: do it. risk is slightly higher transient memory usage but acceptable for mitigation
Sylvie: toggled `--warmup-parallel=6` on 'priority-hotshot'. Observing warmup throughput jump x3
Jordan: once all slots warm, queue should drain. p99 trending down 1.1s -> 700ms
IncidentBot: Incident INC-2026-432 created, severity=P1, priority pool saturation, assigned: Ana M., Mike R., Sylvie, Jordan, Devon
Ana M.: customer comms: CS drafted a short note to affected customers. Should we send now or wait for stable p99 < 500ms?
Mike R.: send now with ETA 30-45m, include that fallback was enabled and we're adding capacity. Keep updates every 10m
Devon: attaching last slot succeeded. warmup success_rate now 0.93
Jordan: queue depth 1800 -> 600 in 6m, streaming stalls reduced in logs
Ana M.: handoff in 25m to nights: @Oncall-SRE will carry paging. We'll open a follow-up to investigate root cause (object-store IO amplification during warmup bursts)
Oncall-SRE: confirmed handoff accepted. Will monitor p95/p99 and customer tickets. Leaving notes: enable fallback policy for pools with warmup-susceptible models, consider pre-warm for scheduled bursts
Sylvie: will open an eng-runtime ticket to add prioritized prefetch + backoff on fetch. Tagging: eng-runtime, infra-storage
Mike R.: action items: 1) postmortem owner Sylvie 2) engineering follow-up on warmup parallelism default 3) CS follow-up note to customers 4) possible infra KMS for faster fetch
Ana M.: thanks all. final status: mitigation stable, p99 at 380ms, p95 at 120ms, queue draining. Leaving incident open for investigation
IncidentBot: auto-pause alerts on this incident for 10m during handoff
Oncall-SRE: acknowledged. will escalate to paging if p99 > 1s again
Ana M.: logging handoff summary in incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-432
Mike R.: good work. :thumbsup:
Sylvie: adding initial RCA notes in ticket
Devon: saving warmup logs and storage traces to artifact bundle
Jordan: will follow up on KV-cache preheat heuristics
Ana M.: handing over, cya. :wave:
